relationships.subject: multiple lesion induction
relationships.evidence_quote: Elevated TRPV1+ and SP+ DRG remained high in the multiple-induction mice at 6 weeks but not in the single-induction mice, while CGRP+ DRG were still high in the single-induction mice at 6 weeks (Figure 7, A and B).

relationships.subject: dienogest
relationships.evidence_quote: Dienogest and fingolimod reduced elevated TRPV1+, SP+, and CGRP+ DRG in the multiple-induction group but not in the single-induction group (Figure 13, A and B).

relationships.subject: fingolimod
relationships.evidence_quote: Dienogest and fingolimod reduced elevated TRPV1+, SP+, and CGRP+ DRG in the multiple-induction group but not in the single-induction group (Figure 13, A and B).

relationships.subject: fingolimod
relationships.evidence_quote: Dienogest and fingolimod improved abdominal sensitivity at 7 weeks (Figure 10C).

relationships.subject: multiple lesion induction
relationships.evidence_quote: Elevated cytokine levels returned to the preinduction levels in the single-induction mice at 6 weeks; however, they remained high in the multiple-induction mice.

key_findings: Repeated lesion induction (retrograde menstruation model) causes persistent glial activation in brain regions, elevated TRPV1, SP and CGRP in DRG, and prolonged peritoneal inflammation.
Dienogest and fingolimod reduced abdominal hyperalgesia, glial activation and DRG TRPV1/SP/CGRP in multiple-induction mice.
